rubric.why: Recognises that chemistry is a complex subject.
rubric.description: Mentions the complexity or wide scope of chemistry.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the complex nature of the subject as a reason for dividing it into branches.

rubric.why: Identifies the purpose of focusing study on particular areas.
rubric.description: States that branches allow concentration on specific aspects of chemistry.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that distinct branches let scientists focus on areas of study.

modelAnswer: To understand the widely spread complex subject of chemistry and to concentrate on its specific aspects, chemistry is divided into many distinct branches. These branches have distinct areas of study for the scientists to focus on and to achieve breakthroughs and advancements.

rubric.why: Names physical chemistry and its focus on substances at atomic and molecular levels.
rubric.description: Identifies physical chemistry as studying behaviour at atomic and molecular levels.
rubric.how: Award for the branch and its atomic/molecular focus.

rubric.why: Names nuclear chemistry and locates the reactions in the atom's nucleus.
rubric.description: Identifies nuclear chemistry as dealing with reactions in the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award for the branch and the location of the reactions.

modelAnswer: Physical chemistry investigates how substances behave at atomic and molecular levels. Nuclear chemistry deals with the reactions taking place in the nucleus of an atom.

rubric.why: Identifies plasma as the state of matter in the Sun.
The textbook answer identifies the Sun's state directly as plasma.
rubric.description: Gives the answer in the context of the Sun.
rubric.how: Award for the correct textbook response, “Plasma.”

rubric.why: Identifies mixtures as the form of matter to which most material things belong.
rubric.description: States that most material things belong to mixtures.

rubric.why: Supports the answer with an everyday example from the textbook.
rubric.description: Gives at least one example of a mixture.
rubric.how: Award for any one correct example, such as air, soil, milk or tap water.

modelAnswer: Mixtures. Air, soil, milk and tap water are everyday examples of mixtures.

rubric.why: Identifies the subject matter of organic chemistry.
rubric.description: States that organic chemistry deals with carbon compounds.
rubric.how: Award for the branch and its focus on carbon compounds.

rubric.why: Identifies biochemistry and its connection to living organisms.
rubric.description: States that biochemistry studies chemical substances and vital processes in living organisms.
rubric.how: Award for naming biochemistry and describing its study of substances or processes in living organisms.

modelAnswer: Organic chemistry deals with carbon compounds, while biochemistry is the study of chemical substances and vital processes occurring in living organisms.

rubric.why: Names the branch that studies chemical and biochemical phenomena in the environment.
States the phenomena and where they occur.
rubric.description: Mentions chemical and biochemical phenomena occurring in the environment or on the planet.
rubric.how: Award for describing the branch's subject of study.

modelAnswer: Environmental chemistry is the scientific study of the chemical and biochemical phenomena that occur in this planet.
